newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields holding reasonably stable.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields holding reasonably stable.

text.p: *Australian bond yields held reasonably stable during a modestly traded morning session as the market cast its eye offshore in the aftermath of Friday's sell-off in U.S. stocks.
Australian bond yields held reasonably stable during a modestly traded morning session as the market kept a wary eye offshore in the aftermath of Friday's plunge in U.S. stocks.

The local share market fell around 2.0 percent from Friday's close following the 247 point dive in the Dow Jones industrial average on Friday, but analysts feel it will be the U.S. performance on Monday which will determine whether domestic financial markets will be destined for a shake-up.
"Any further weakness will inevitably flow through to our domestic market," said David Lansley, treasury economist at NAB.

For bonds the key event will be Tuesday's Reserve Bank quarterly bulletin, although its impact has been somewhat watered down by RBA governor Ian Macfarlane's speech last week which was less hawkish than expected and appeared to put little weight on wage growth fears.

"If there is some indication from the Reserve Bank that they see the risks of both wages growth and inflation on the low side then that will keep the window open for a possible easing down the line," said Stephen Halmarick, bond and currency strategist at County NatWest Australia.
Bill futures are already beginning to factor in an easing.

December bill futures are staying close to last week's contract peak which followed a benign set of final second quarter wages data and at 95.25 are indicating a cash rate of 4.75 percent compared with official 5.0 percent rates.
Long dated bond yields see-sawed around Friday's closing levels as the market attempted to consolidate after last week's wild fluctuations which were largely U.S. driven.
U.S. Treasuries were trading around Friday's mixed New York levels in early Tokyo trading.

Yield differentials to the dollar bloc remained mixed with the local market giving up some ground to the U.S. after the strong outperformance late last week. The market outpaced New Zealand, although there was minimal reaction in the debt market after the RBNZ said monetary policy conditions were too loose.
